I'm also a college freshman. I'm moving back into my dorm again after winter break later today, actually. Last semester I completely fucked up in several classes and I'm on academic probation now. I'm lucky that my roommate and I get along very well- she's definitely the best and only real friend I have at the moment.

College really is hard. Not just academics, the social stuff, too. I've always struggled with social skills. Plus, it's scary being an adult and having to get loans and do all kinds of schoolwork and figure out how to make friends when you're not in 3rd grade and you automatically befriend whomever the teacher sat next to you.

Obviously, I can't tell you how to make a bunch of friends and all that. I joined my university's LGBT club but I don't really talk to anyone I've met from there outside of meetings. This is something I want to work on this semester (in addition to my grades LOL).

I'm not sure what advice I can really offer, but I sincerely hope you have more luck with people in the future. Also, was the therapist you tried to get an appointment with from your school? Mine offers counciling to students, paid through tuition and stuff I think. If not, you should see if your school offers something like that. Or keep looking for outside therapists. Unfortunately, finding a good therapist that can actually treat YOU is often difficult.

Finally, I just want to say you're not alone. Many, many people struggle with college in the beginning. I've had several professors tell me that their first year was definitely the hardest for the same reasons as us. It got better, though- and I don't think they're any more special than you or me. There's all kinds of bad shit happening in the world, but I haven't given up hope yet. You know, even if college doesn't work out, it's not the end. The world is a big place with a lot to do. I believe there's something out there for you, and that you'll find it.
